what: The ADMISSION RECORD of the INSTRUCT-DIRECT ('it-doc') batch-64 re-fit objects (the eight-arm extension, it-doc wave): one entry per (lane, model key, view, cell id) -> object sha256. The pin is the OBJECT's sha256 (64-hex), read on disk at full length (never from a message); a row LAUNCHES only when its entry carries the pin AND its RULED staged id AND a complete `bank` binding (the bank view relative to the shared root per cluster role + the cell dir) AND no hold_reason — anything less is HELD with the reason, never a placeholder sha. At launch the row's bytes are held to the pin at four doors (itdoc_bind.bind_problems: manifest entry + disk bytes + sidecar of the kind + the pin file's (target, staged id); the standup's and the driver's --expect-object-sha256; the driver's provenance mirror). A cell id is NOT unique across lanes and a staged id is not unique across targets: every lookup keys the full tuple.
qualification: the CONSTITUTION cell is BUDGET-LIMITED, NOT CONVERGED — best_epoch 16 of 16 with stopped_early False, so its best held-out CE was the last epoch and the budget bound the result (a box-edge argmin, treated as a selection failure elsewhere in this campaign); the CONTROL early-stopped at best_epoch 1 of 3; any difference of the pair inherits this asymmetry; nobody is re-fitting for it
qualification_scope: `qualification` = the model's OWN sentence, VERBATIM (qwen: the pair sentence the brief fixed; gemma: the cross-model pattern sentence, its numbers 16/16 and 4/6); `qualification_pattern` = the PATTERN across both models, VERBATIM, on every row of either model. Both travel with every row and every result; state them, never smooth them.
